newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Moody's assigns ratings to Donghwa Bank.
newsitem.headline: Moody's assigns ratings to Donghwa Bank.

text.p: Moody's Investors Services said on Thursday it had assigned the following first-time ratings to South Korea's Donghwa Bank -
Moody's said the rating's reflected Donghwa Bank's "very weak franchises and its poor financial fundamentals".
It said the bank was less likely than other South Korean banks to receive assistance from regulators if needed.
Donghwa Bank was established in Seoul in 1989 and had consolidated assets of 11,086 billion won as of the end of December 1995.
Moody's said the bank, which operates 115 branches in South Korea and one in New York, lacks the stable and cheap base of its older and larger competitors.
It was required to make make large provisionals against impaired loans and securities losses and it reported a net loss for 1995 and a smaller loss in the first half of 1996.
Its problems have prompted a management restructuring which is under way, Moody's said, but gave no details.
